title: Vanuatu adopts SMB1001 as its national cybersecurity baseline, SecurityBrief reports
date_note: SecurityBrief Australia's article of 27 November reports the adoption; the page gives no earlier day.
geo_basis: the article names the Government of Vanuatu; pin at the national capital Port Vila, not stated by the page
summary: The Government of Vanuatu has signed a sovereign-level licence with Dynamic Standards International (DSI) to adopt the SMB1001 standard for small and medium-sized organisations as its national cybersecurity baseline, SecurityBrief reports. The article describes it as the first national government to use the standard this way. DSI is providing the standard at no cost.
plain: Vanuatu's government has adopted a small-business cybersecurity standard, SMB1001, as its national baseline, SecurityBrief reports. It is the first national government to do so, the article says.
exec: SecurityBrief reports a national government now uses SMB1001 as its baseline; the licence also lets it create its own assessment scheme and authorise local certifiers later.

validation.note: One publisher group (SecurityBrief/IT Brief/ChannelLife, same article syndicated); the government's and DSI's own releases were not read.
